# Archify Diagram Skill for Muse

Turns plain-language system descriptions — or pasted Mermaid flowcharts, sequence diagrams, and state diagrams — into polished, explorable architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle/state diagrams delivered as standalone HTML files with inline SVG, dark and light themes, optional trace-motion animation, and export to PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, or WebM. It authors from a typed JSON schema with example-driven layout rules, then runs a gated finalize pipeline — showcase validation, strict checks, and a real-browser check — with bounded repair reruns when a gate fails, and it can trace real repository evidence when the diagram must reflect actual code rather than a description. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: the full pipeline needs Node.js and the bundled archify CLI that ships with the skill package; the skill is opinionated about process (fresh IDs and wording per diagram, automatic routing first, no preliminary drafts), and without shell access it falls back to hand-placed SVG, which is slower and less validated. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
